title: Genetics, Inheritance, and Variation Core Test
description: Core practice for chromosomes, genes, traits, inherited information, environment, and variation.

questions.prompt: A pea plant has chromosomes in its cells. Which statement best describes chromosomes?
questions.questionText: A pea plant has chromosomes in its cells. Which statement best describes chromosomes?
options: Chromosomes carry many genes that influence traits.
Chromosomes are only food molecules.
Chromosomes are the same as sunlight.
Chromosomes are nonliving rocks inside soil.
questions.correctAnswer: Chromosomes carry many genes that influence traits.
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are structures that carry genes, and genes influence traits.

questions.prompt: Two related tomato plants both inherited information for tall growth, but one receives little water. Which outcome is most reasonable?
questions.questionText: Two related tomato plants both inherited information for tall growth, but one receives little water. Which outcome is most reasonable?
options: The low-water plant must change all of its genes.
The low-water plant may grow shorter because environment affects trait expression.
Water cannot affect any observed trait.
The plant with little water stops having cells.
questions.correctAnswer: The low-water plant may grow shorter because environment affects trait expression.
questions.explanation: An inherited growth pattern can be affected by environmental resources such as water.

questions.prompt: Which model best shows how inherited information can affect a trait?
questions.questionText: Which model best shows how inherited information can affect a trait?
options: trait -> sunlight -> chromosome disappears
cell wall -> soil color -> no genes
chromosomes -> genes -> cell processes -> trait
organism chooses gene -> instant trait
questions.correctAnswer: chromosomes -> genes -> cell processes -> trait
questions.explanation: Genes on chromosomes influence cell processes that can affect traits.

questions.prompt: A class measures plant heights from the same seed variety grown with different light levels. Which claim can the data help test?
questions.questionText: A class measures plant heights from the same seed variety grown with different light levels. Which claim can the data help test?
options: Light creates chromosomes from nothing.
All plants must become identical.
Measurements cannot be evidence.
Light can affect how much the inherited growth potential is expressed.
questions.correctAnswer: Light can affect how much the inherited growth potential is expressed.
questions.explanation: Comparing growth under different light levels can test an environmental effect on an observed trait.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains variation?
questions.questionText: Which statement best explains variation?
options: Variation means individuals in a group are not all exactly alike.
Variation means every organism is identical.
Variation means traits are never inherited.
Variation means environments do not matter.
questions.correctAnswer: Variation means individuals in a group are not all exactly alike.
questions.explanation: Variation is the presence of differences among individuals.

questions.prompt: A student says, "If a trait is inherited, the environment cannot affect it." Which evidence best challenges the statement?
questions.questionText: A student says, "If a trait is inherited, the environment cannot affect it." Which evidence best challenges the statement?
options: All plants are green.
Plants with similar inherited information grow to different heights when water differs.
Genes are found on chromosomes.
A pot can be plastic.
Some leaves are wide.
questions.correctAnswer: Plants with similar inherited information grow to different heights when water differs.
questions.explanation: The evidence shows the environment can affect how an inherited trait appears.

questions.prompt: A model shows gene A affects pigment production in flower cells. What does the model help explain?
questions.questionText: A model shows gene A affects pigment production in flower cells. What does the model help explain?
options: why flowers are not made of cells
why traits are unrelated to genes
how a gene can influence a visible trait through a cell process
why soil always decides flower color
why chromosomes are outside organisms
questions.correctAnswer: how a gene can influence a visible trait through a cell process
questions.explanation: The model connects a gene to a cell process and then to a trait.

questions.prompt: Which investigation best separates inherited and environmental influences on plant height?
questions.questionText: Which investigation best separates inherited and environmental influences on plant height?
options: Ask which plant looks nicest.
Measure one plant once without recording conditions.
Use different seeds, different soil, different light, and different water all at once.
Grow the same plant variety under different water conditions and compare height.
questions.correctAnswer: Grow the same plant variety under different water conditions and compare height.
questions.explanation: Changing one environmental factor while keeping inherited background similar makes the test stronger.

questions.prompt: A family of dogs includes puppies with different fur shades. Which explanation fits Grade 7 genetics best without assuming the environment did everything?
questions.questionText: A family of dogs includes puppies with different fur shades. Which explanation fits Grade 7 genetics best without assuming the environment did everything?
options: Related organisms can inherit different combinations of genetic information.
All related organisms must be identical.
Fur shade is never connected to inherited information.
Dogs choose chromosome combinations after birth.
questions.correctAnswer: Related organisms can inherit different combinations of genetic information.
questions.explanation: Related organisms can share inherited information but still show variation.

questions.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes inherited information from an acquired feature?
questions.questionText: Which statement best distinguishes inherited information from an acquired feature?
options: A scar is always a gene.
A gene affecting natural fur color is inherited; a scar from an injury is acquired.
Natural fur color cannot be inherited.
Acquired features are passed through chromosomes.
questions.correctAnswer: A gene affecting natural fur color is inherited; a scar from an injury is acquired.
questions.explanation: Inherited traits are connected to genetic information; acquired features happen during life.

questions.prompt: A table shows four related plants with leaf widths of 4 cm, 5 cm, 5 cm, and 7 cm. What does the table show?
questions.questionText: A table shows four related plants with leaf widths of 4 cm, 5 cm, 5 cm, and 7 cm. What does the table show?
options: All plants have identical leaves.
Leaf width cannot be measured.
There is variation in leaf width among related plants.
No trait can vary within a group.
questions.correctAnswer: There is variation in leaf width among related plants.
questions.explanation: The measurements are not all the same, so they show variation.

questions.prompt: Which claim is best supported if two groups of the same plant variety grow differently in high-nutrient and low-nutrient soil?
questions.questionText: Which claim is best supported if two groups of the same plant variety grow differently in high-nutrient and low-nutrient soil?
options: Nutrients are chromosomes.
Inherited information is impossible to study.
All growth differences prove the plants are unrelated.
Nutrient availability can affect observed growth.
questions.correctAnswer: Nutrient availability can affect observed growth.
questions.explanation: A difference between nutrient conditions can support an environmental influence on growth.

questions.prompt: Why are models useful for genetics?
questions.questionText: Why are models useful for genetics?
options: They can show relationships among chromosomes, genes, cell processes, and traits.
They prove every trait has only one cause.
They replace the need for evidence.
They show that traits are unrelated to cells.
questions.correctAnswer: They can show relationships among chromosomes, genes, cell processes, and traits.
questions.explanation: A genetics model helps connect invisible inherited information to observable traits.

questions.prompt: Which example best shows a trait influenced by both inherited information and environment?
questions.questionText: Which example best shows a trait influenced by both inherited information and environment?
options: A rock becomes smoother in a river.
A plant variety can grow tall, but drought keeps many plants shorter.
A desk is painted blue.
A shadow changes shape during the day.
questions.correctAnswer: A plant variety can grow tall, but drought keeps many plants shorter.
questions.explanation: The plant has inherited growth potential, but water availability affects the observed height.

questions.prompt: A student claims, "One example proves a trait is controlled only by genes." What is the best scientific response?
questions.questionText: A student claims, "One example proves a trait is controlled only by genes." What is the best scientific response?
options: One example is always enough.
Do not collect data.
Use data from many individuals and consider environmental conditions too.
Ignore the environment in every investigation.
questions.correctAnswer: Use data from many individuals and consider environmental conditions too.
questions.explanation: Stronger claims use patterns across multiple data points and control possible variables.

questions.prompt: Which evidence best supports that a trait has an inherited influence?
questions.questionText: Which evidence best supports that a trait has an inherited influence?
options: One organism changed color under a lamp.
The trait was hard to spell.
The organism lived near a window.
Related organisms show similar patterns for the trait across many examples.
questions.correctAnswer: Related organisms show similar patterns for the trait across many examples.
questions.explanation: Repeated similarity among related organisms can support inherited influence.

questions.prompt: A diagram shows chromosomes inside the nucleus. Which statement best interprets the diagram?
questions.questionText: A diagram shows chromosomes inside the nucleus. Which statement best interprets the diagram?
options: Genetic information is stored inside cells, not floating outside the organism.
Genes are stored only in soil.
Chromosomes are outside all cells.
The nucleus is unrelated to inherited information.
questions.correctAnswer: Genetic information is stored inside cells, not floating outside the organism.
questions.explanation: Chromosomes carrying genes are found inside cells, often in the nucleus of plant and animal cells.

questions.prompt: A crop scientist compares two plant varieties in the same field. One variety remains shorter in every watered section. Which explanation is most reasonable?
questions.questionText: A crop scientist compares two plant varieties in the same field. One variety remains shorter in every watered section. Which explanation is most reasonable?
options: Water must be the only factor.
Inherited differences between varieties may influence height.
The shorter plants do not contain cells.
All varieties have exactly the same genes.
questions.correctAnswer: Inherited differences between varieties may influence height.
questions.explanation: When environment is similar, inherited differences may explain a consistent trait pattern.

questions.prompt: Which question would most improve an investigation of environment and traits?
questions.questionText: Which question would most improve an investigation of environment and traits?
options: Were the plant labels pretty?
Did the classroom have a clock?
Were the plants from the same variety and grown with only one condition changed?
Did the scientist like tall plants better?
questions.correctAnswer: Were the plants from the same variety and grown with only one condition changed?
questions.explanation: A fair test controls inherited background and changes one environmental variable.

questions.prompt: A trait-frequency chart shows 70% dark shells and 30% light shells in one snail population. What can the chart show?
questions.questionText: A trait-frequency chart shows 70% dark shells and 30% light shells in one snail population. What can the chart show?
options: which snail chose its shell color
that environment never matters
that chromosomes disappeared
the pattern of variation for shell color in the population
questions.correctAnswer: the pattern of variation for shell color in the population
questions.explanation: Trait-frequency data can describe variation within a population.

questions.prompt: Why is it incomplete to say, "Genes make traits"?
questions.questionText: Why is it incomplete to say, "Genes make traits"?
options: Genes influence traits through cell processes, and environment can also affect observed traits.
Genes are never involved in traits.
Environment creates all chromosomes.
Traits cannot be explained with models.
questions.correctAnswer: Genes influence traits through cell processes, and environment can also affect observed traits.
questions.explanation: A stronger explanation includes pathways and possible environmental influences.

questions.prompt: A model shows inherited information plus sunlight and water affecting plant height. What kind of trait explanation is this?
questions.questionText: A model shows inherited information plus sunlight and water affecting plant height. What kind of trait explanation is this?
options: a genes-only explanation
a both-genes-and-environment explanation
an environment-only explanation
a nonliving-rock explanation
questions.correctAnswer: a both-genes-and-environment explanation
questions.explanation: The model includes both inherited and environmental factors.

questions.prompt: Which data would weaken the claim that water alone determines plant height?
questions.questionText: Which data would weaken the claim that water alone determines plant height?
options: Plants need water.
A ruler measures centimeters.
With equal water, different plant varieties still grow to different average heights.
Low-water plants are sometimes shorter.
questions.correctAnswer: With equal water, different plant varieties still grow to different average heights.
questions.explanation: If height differs when water is equal, other factors such as inherited information may matter.

questions.prompt: A student sees that two related plants have different leaf spots and says one must be unhealthy. What is a better first explanation to test?
questions.questionText: A student sees that two related plants have different leaf spots and says one must be unhealthy. What is a better first explanation to test?
options: Any difference always means disease.
Related organisms cannot vary.
Traits never need evidence.
The spots may be normal variation, but evidence is needed before deciding.
questions.correctAnswer: The spots may be normal variation, but evidence is needed before deciding.
questions.explanation: Variation can be normal, and scientific conclusions should use evidence.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best uses the chain chromosomes -> genes -> traits?
questions.questionText: Which explanation best uses the chain chromosomes -> genes -> traits?
options: Chromosomes carry genes; genes influence cell processes; cell processes can affect traits.
Traits carry chromosomes outside cells.
Genes are the same as all environments.
Chromosomes are made only when traits are measured.
questions.correctAnswer: Chromosomes carry genes; genes influence cell processes; cell processes can affect traits.
questions.explanation: The chain connects inherited information to observable traits.

questions.prompt: A plant has genes for purple flowers but produces pale flowers in poor soil. What is the best explanation?
questions.questionText: A plant has genes for purple flowers but produces pale flowers in poor soil. What is the best explanation?
options: Poor soil changed every chromosome into water.
The inherited trait pattern may be affected by environmental conditions.
Genes cannot influence color.
Flower color proves the plant is nonliving.
questions.correctAnswer: The inherited trait pattern may be affected by environmental conditions.
questions.explanation: Environmental conditions can affect how an inherited trait appears.

questions.prompt: Which is the strongest claim for a genetics investigation?
questions.questionText: Which is the strongest claim for a genetics investigation?
options: The tallest plant proves all traits are environmental.
Genes are never involved.
The data suggest both inherited variety and light level affected plant height.
One plant proves all plant growth rules.
questions.correctAnswer: The data suggest both inherited variety and light level affected plant height.
questions.explanation: The strongest claim is careful and matches evidence without overgeneralizing.

questions.prompt: A student wants to explain why related organisms are similar but not identical. Which idea is most important?
questions.questionText: A student wants to explain why related organisms are similar but not identical. Which idea is most important?
options: They have no inherited information.
They must all live in identical environments.
They cannot show variation.
They share some inherited information but can have different combinations and environmental experiences.
questions.correctAnswer: They share some inherited information but can have different combinations and environmental experiences.
questions.explanation: Similarity and variation can both be explained by inherited information and environment.

questions.prompt: Which review statement best captures genetics and variation?
questions.questionText: Which review statement best captures genetics and variation?
options: Genes on chromosomes influence traits, and variation comes from inherited differences plus environmental effects.
Genes are unrelated to traits.
Environment never changes observed traits.
All related organisms are identical.
questions.correctAnswer: Genes on chromosomes influence traits, and variation comes from inherited differences plus environmental effects.
questions.explanation: This statement connects genes, chromosomes, traits, variation, and environment.

questions.prompt: Which evidence should make a scientist revise a simple genes-only model for a trait?
questions.questionText: Which evidence should make a scientist revise a simple genes-only model for a trait?
options: The model has arrows.
The same plant variety shows different trait values under different temperatures.
The plants are measured in centimeters.
The trait has a name.
questions.correctAnswer: The same plant variety shows different trait values under different temperatures.
questions.explanation: Environmental temperature affecting the same variety suggests the model needs environment too.
